items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: So they got him to come down and hear me. So he gave me a talking... And anyway, I joined the band, Ernie Fields' band.

ctx.x: So in the meantime, I am still working over at Wat Sanders' Blue Room. And another old friend of mine, Wild Bill Moore, appeared in town with Christine Chapman, the lady...a fine boogie-woogie pianist. She had a big hit at the time called "Naptown Boogie" -- she was out of Indianapolis. So it was nice to see Wild Bill again.

So I'm still doing my trip, and Ernie Fields' Orchestra came to town. And some of the guys came down to the Blue Room and heard me play. They would come in every night. They must have been around there four or five days, and they'd come in and they'd listen to me play. So they went back and really vouched for me to join the band, you know, with Ernie Fields -- talked to Ernie about me. So they got him to come down and hear me. So he gave me a talking... items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Teddy Edwards was in your band... I sent back later and got Jack and Teddy Edwards... I turned the reed section over to him and he worked with the guys.

ctx.x: I hope we have enough tape so we won't have to interrupt, one of the most interesting stories is the story of how "In The Mood" happened.
Well, before you go talking about that, I want to mention one more man before we got onto "In The Mood".

You spoke about him before, Teddy Edwards. Teddy Edwards--I had a habit--I don't have a lot, you know you can't take it with you, but I think I would have been more successful with money if I could just pass up a good musician, but when I saw a good one I couldn't pass it up. Do you know King Kolax?
